qs.q: What is a key diagnostic clue for chronic pyelonephritis, distinguishing it from other kidney diseases?
o: Presence of classic nephrotic syndrome
Involvement of the calyces and pelvis
Total absence of interstitial inflammation
Symmetric scarring of the renal cortex
qs.e: The note emphasizes that 'only chronic pyelonephritis and analgesic nephropathy affect the calyces — pelvocalyceal damage is a diagnostic clue'. Glomerulonephritis causes symmetric scarring, and TIN is characterized by interstitial inflammation.
qs.s: Acute Tubular Injury (ATI): AKI Causes, Pathology & Prognosis: MCQs

qs.q: What is a key morphological hallmark that helps distinguish chronic pyelonephritis from other chronic renal diseases?
o: Diffuse calcium deposition in the loops of Henle
Symmetric global glomerular sclerosis
Pelvocalyceal damage with deformed calyces
Exclusive involvement of the renal cortex
qs.e: Chronic pyelonephritis and analgesic nephropathy uniquely affect the calyces, making pelvocalyceal damage a key diagnostic clue. Glomerulonephritis, by contrast, typically presents with symmetric renal involvement.
qs.s: Acute Tubular Injury (ATI): AKI Causes, Pathology & Prognosis: MCQs

qs.q: What microscopic feature characterizes the 'thyroidization' seen in chronic pyelonephritis?
o: Necrotic pyramid tips with preserved tubule outlines
Granulomas containing foamy giant cells
Hyperplastic thyroid-like follicular cells in the interstitium
Dilated tubules filled with casts resembling thyroid colloid
qs.e: Thyroidization refers to dilated tubules filled with casts that resemble thyroid colloid in chronic pyelonephritis. This is accompanied by interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy.
qs.s: Acute Tubular Injury (ATI): AKI Causes, Pathology & Prognosis: MCQs

qs.q: What is the clinical significance of secondary focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) developing with proteinuria in advanced chronic pyelonephritis?
o: It confirms the absence of underlying hypertension
It represents a purely benign finding of tubular hypertrophy
It indicates spontaneous disease remission
It is a poor prognostic sign pointing toward ESRD
qs.e: Secondary FSGS with significant proteinuria is a poor prognostic sign that strongly suggests progression to end-stage renal disease. It is seen in advanced cases of chronic pyelonephritis.
qs.s: Acute Tubular Injury (ATI): AKI Causes, Pathology & Prognosis: MCQs

qs.q: Which clinical feature is characteristic of chronic pyelonephritis due to the loss of renal concentrating ability?
o: Polyuria and frequent nocturia
Frank gross hematuria
Oliguria and total anuria
Acute urinary retention
qs.e: Patients with chronic pyelonephritis often present with polyuria and nocturia resulting from the loss of renal concentrating ability. Late presentations may also feature renal insufficiency and hypertension.
qs.s: Acute Tubular Injury (ATI): AKI Causes, Pathology & Prognosis: MCQs
